what: XPeng makes electric cars in China, with a focus on driver assistance software it develops itself, and it is also building flying vehicles and humanoid robots.
customers: Chinese buyers of mid-priced electric cars, sold through its own stores.
money: the G, P and M series electric cars and the Mona brand
software, charging and the technology agreement with Volkswagen
moat: Driver assistance software developed in-house rather than bought in, which it now also licenses to Volkswagen, giving it a technology revenue stream other Chinese carmakers lack.
risks: A $468M net loss and $2.2B of negative free cash flow
Chinese electric vehicle price competition is severe
Flying cars and robots consume cash with no near-term revenue
opportunities: Revenue nearly doubled from $5.6B to $11.0B last year as the cheaper Mona range sold well
Analysts see about 71% upside, and the Volkswagen platform agreement pays regardless of its own car sales
watch: Monthly deliveries and the gross margin per vehicle.
